science.assessment: Fixed amount/composition, equilibrium states, absolute pressure and kelvin temperature are explicit. Simultaneous variation is not mislabeled as isothermal/isobaric. Ice-in-ball observation is conditional on shell elasticity and negligible leakage/water-vapor composition changes; pressure/volume decrease is possible, not asserted as a universal gas law.

Initial/final equilibrium states and the illustrative intermediate state are distinct. The stated route consists of consecutive isobaric heating/expansion to temperature T2, then slow isothermal compression in the same bath; heat exchange and intermediate equilibrium are explicit. It is not two alternative methods or an adiabatic compression. Elimination of V' from (2-10)/(2-11)/(2-12) correctly gives (2-13); the state relation does not require every actual process to follow the illustrative path. Subfigure references a/b/c and paths1-1'/1'-2 retain their roles; pixels remain unreviewed.

The fixed-quantity invariant is distinguished from universal R and from arbitrary gas amount. V_mu is correctly defined as molar volume, not arbitrary total volume; nu=m/mu has compatible mass/molar-mass units and V=nu V_mu has volume units. Pa times cubic metres per mole per kelvin yields J/(mol K); erg conversion is correct. The (2-17) to (2-19) derivation and final two-known-state-parameter claim correctly require known gas amount/composition. Real-gas use is qualified by the ideal-gas approximation.

Source-bound Clapeyron/Mendeleev identities, dates, locations, equation names, periodic law, gas/liquid work and industrial topics remain with item-specific historical_entities. Propagandistic praise is removed without replacing the historical subject. Critical-temperature prose correctly limits the claim to liquefaction by pressure alone above the critical temperature; no new measured data or archival-authenticity claim.

science.assessment: Original title/history/year1787 and footnote remain. Main prose avoids misattributing the isochoric result to the historical experiment; footnote explicitly concerns constant-pressure volume/temperature work. The source naming convention is retained without confusing it with the footnote's law. Theory does not replace experimental checking of real gases/apparatus. Historical names and France are individually declared.

Fixed gas amount/composition/volume, equilibrium endpoints, absolute pressure and kelvin temperature correctly support (2-20)/(2-21). Celsius readings and gauge pressures are explicitly excluded from direct proportionality. Isochoric-line comparison requires the same gas amount and same absolute temperature; larger volume gives smaller pressure and slope. Figure-text relationship is mathematically correct without inspecting pixels.

The ambiguous original simultaneous-zero sentence is clarified narratively into different constrained model limits: fixed positive volume gives pressure tending to zero; fixed nonzero pressure gives volume tending to zero. Fixed volume does not vanish. The origin is an ideal-model extrapolation, not a reachable real-gas state; possible liquefaction is stated. No original mathematical expression was altered and no extrapolated measurement was invented.

Both original prose proof requests remain, without new exercises or worked answers. The first preserves p=p0 gamma T and specifies fixed amount/composition/volume. p0 is the pressure of that same gas and volume at the source273K reference; gamma uses that fixed reference denominator, not arbitrary starting pressure. K^-1 is a temperature-difference inverse; Celsius/K differences have equal sizes but Celsius readings are not absolute temperatures. The final prompt correctly pairs fixed temperature with Boyle-Mariotte and fixed pressure with Gay-Lussac, retaining references(2-19)/(2-2)/(2-7).

numerical_check.independent_derivation: At fixed amount and volume let C=mR/(mu V). Then p=C T and p0=C T0 imply gamma=1/T0 and pressure increment/reference pressure = deltaT/T0. With the source's integer referenceT0=273K, 1/273 = 0.003663003663003663 K^-1. This explains the source approximation and reference-denominator wording; it is review reasoning, not an added product formula or solved exercise.
numerical_check.approximation: Equality of pressure/volume coefficients is interpreted within the explicitly retained integer273 approximation, not a new exact identification of273K with modern0 degrees Celsius.
